clean_body: EMILYs List women are ready to take on these MAGA Republicans | = Peter, What do Mariannette Miller-Meeks, Anna Paulina Luna, and Derrick Van Orden have in common? They're all vulnerable MAGA Republican incumbents — and EMILYs List women are running to defeat every one of them this November. The tide is turning. Our candidates are competing in some of the most important red-to-blue races in the country, with control of the U.S. House and Senate hanging in the balance. = | = Here's who our women are up against: Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01) barely won reelection in 2024 — and has spent her time in Congress attacking reproductive freedom and voting to cut affordable healthcare for her constituents. She's co-sponsored a national abortion ban, urged the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn Roe v. Wade , and voted against protecting access to contraception. Christina Bohannan is running to defeat her once and for all. Derrick Van Orden (WI-03) attended the Jan. 6 rally, continues to deny the results of the 2020 election, and has championed an agenda that benefits the wealthy at the expense of working families. Rebecca Cooke came close to defeating him in 2024 — and she's ready to finish the job this year. Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) has called herself a "pro-life extremist," introduced legislation to put Donald Trump's face on Mount Rushmore, and supported his reckless agenda in Congress. Retired Army Brigadier General Leela Gray is ready to replace her with real leadership. Christina, Rebecca, and Leela all have what it takes to defeat these dangerous Republicans and help Democrats take back power in Congress. A record of directing his taxpayer-funded staff, on taxpayer-funded time, to apply for and solicit cash prizes for himself. It's sick. For someone who called himself the most famous scientist in the world, which he did, Fauci has done more harm to science than any single person in the past 50 years. ### Hey Peter,
---
| | Today is World Day Against Trafficking in Persons. In remote India, trafficking is deeply tied to poverty. When families can't afford basic necessities, some feel forced to send their children away to work, or in the most desperate situations, to sell them outright. Other children are picked up off the streets when they're unsupervised and vulnerable. In almost every case, it comes back to the same root problem, a family trapped in a cycle of poverty.
---
| |
## Nearly 79 percent of all child trafficking cases in India involve labor exploitation, and every year, tens of thousands of children go missing.
---
| | Sponsorship changes that math. When a child is sponsored, their family has one less impossible choice to make. They have food on the table every day. They receive regular medical care. And they are provided with school supplies, so they can begin walking toward a better future. Poverty no longer has the power to push these children toward a trafficker's door.
---

clean_body: On World Day Against Trafficking, a look at what actually changes a child's path. | | | | | | | | | | | Hey Peter, | | Today is World Day Against Trafficking in Persons. In remote India, trafficking is deeply tied to poverty. When families can't afford basic necessities, some feel forced to send their children away to work, or in the most desperate situations, to sell them outright. Other children are picked up off the streets when they're unsupervised and vulnerable. In almost every case, it comes back to the same root problem, a family trapped in a cycle of poverty. | | Nearly 79 percent of all child trafficking cases in India involve labor exploitation, and every year, tens of thousands of children go missing. | | Sponsorship changes that math. When a child is sponsored, their family has one less impossible choice to make. They have food on the table every day. They receive regular medical care. And they are provided with school supplies, so they can begin walking toward a better future. Poverty no longer has the power to push these children toward a trafficker's door. | | Not a sponsor, yet? Click below to sponsor a child today! | | | While sponsorship is prevention against trafficking, it is also rescue. In one of the villages we serve, we are partnered with a safe house. This house is a refuge for girls rescued from temple prostitution, a practice that, despite being illegal, still pulls young girls from vulnerable families into a lifetime of exploitation. Through sponsorship and generous donations, these children are given new lives and hope for happy futures. The stories of these especially vulnerable children remind us that this work is both prevention and redemption. | | | Watch the video below for a word from our founder and president, Sean Feucht! | | | You Can Fight Trafficking | | Join us on a live Zoom call today at 12pm PT/3pm ET as our Light A Candle team takes a real look at human trafficking and how it affects our work in India. | | | | Today, we're asking you to do three things. Pray for the children and families in our program, and for the pastors and staff on the ground doing this work every day. If you don't already, consider And if you already sponsor a child, share this with someone who might want to join the LAC sponsorship family! Every new sponsorship is one more life changed. Thank you for continuing to stand with us in this work and proving that the darkness has not overcome the Light in remote India. \- The Light a Candle Team | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Light a Candle PO Box 850382 Richardson, Texas 75085 * USA |

clean_body: "I hope Darline does this." I am in, President Trump! | Peter, With less than three weeks to go, The legacy my brother, Lindsey, built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did, every single day, for the people of South Carolina. Last week, President Trump encouraged me to run in the upcoming Senate Special Election by saying: "Run, Darline, Run!" That endorsement isn't just an honor. It's a call to action. The President knows South Carolina needs a fighter who will finish what my brother started, and he's counting on us to deliver. I intend to earn every vote because that's what this job demands, and that's what South Carolina deserves. But here's the truth: My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years stockpiling campaign cash. I'm new to this. The Special Election Primary is August 11th - just 18 days away. Every dollar raised between now and then determines whether we can compete on the airwaves, get out the vote, and win. There is no "catching up later." This is the moment. President Trump believes in this campaign. Thank you, Darline Graham United States Senator (R-SC) | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? | [](https://substack.com/redirect/bba8b8ba-39b5-4019-b1db-8320d8335b28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_This abandoned watchtower is one of the few structures left from the Lourdes spy base in Cuba. Photo: Reed Lindsay._
_This story was written in collaboration with**[Belly of the Beast](https://substack.com/redirect/9192408f-88da-492c-b44e-5c4c117c830a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , an independent media outlet that covers Cuba and U.S.-Cuba relations. You can support their work on [Patreon](https://substack.com/redirect/1d095e5d-5256-4174-a9e6-8f1b90b4c02a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
Since U.S. President Donald Trump imposed an executive order in January threatening tariffs on any country that ships fuel to Cuba, major media outlets have descended on the island to report on the resulting [prolonged blackouts](https://substack.com/redirect/cbeecdcd-5ca6-48a8-9901-9056534c06e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [collapsing hospitals](https://substack.com/redirect/7ededd66-6653-403f-a5f6-f7382c7fc4d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [piles of uncollected trash](https://substack.com/redirect/f4504650-d6ea-41a2-84e8-2195a8134cf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Far less attention has been paid to the rationale the administration offered for imposing the blockade in the first place.
The [executive order](https://substack.com/redirect/6de89029-80f3-4b7a-a96d-9e3329d924ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) states that Cuba represents a "national emergency" and poses an "unusual and extraordinary threat" to the United States, stringing together a kitchen-sink list of familiar allegations, including accusations that Cuba sponsors terrorism and aligns itself with "dangerous adversaries" of the United States, such as Iran, Hamas, Russia, and China.
More specifically, the order claims that "Cuba hosts Russia's largest overseas signals intelligence facility, which tries to steal sensitive national security information of the United States."
For two months, the allegation that Cuba was hosting a major Russian spy base was largely ignored by U.S. media outlets. Then, on March 24, The New York Times published an[ article](https://substack.com/redirect/59097edc-9ce5-41b3-9a12-0d99f06e1f72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Michael Crowley claiming not only that the Russian spy base exists, but that it "bristles with antennas and other eavesdropping equipment" capable of spying on the U.S. Central Command, the satellite launchpads of Cape Canaveral, and Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence.
Crowley [pinpointed](https://substack.com/redirect/a6ee02f4-7da2-462e-a1f2-43bacdd9084d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the location: a former Soviet base on the outskirts of Havana called Lourdes that was "temporarily shut" by Vladimir Putin in 2001 but was reopened in 2014, according to the Times.
There is just one problem with this story: the base isn't there.
The State Department did not respond to a request for comment. Belly of the Beast also sent requests to The New York Times and to Michael Crowley but received no response.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d3296e4a-ed48-4f80-b86c-f6c3eeb4a448?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Today, Lourdes (also known as Torrens) is home to Cuba's University of Computer Sciences (UCI). [The reporting team at Belly of the Beast](https://substack.com/redirect/9e9d95bb-da49-4939-aef7-56b37b86a7ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**** spent the better part of two days walking the campus, searching the grounds, and speaking with students, faculty, and workers. We found no evidence of an active Russian intelligence base, much less the sort of extensive equipment described by the Times.
"Do I look like a Russian spy?" laughed Malcolm Jarrozai, a 40-year-old art professor who has been teaching at UCI and living at a residence on campus since 2006. "It's truly laughable that these kinds of claims are being made and that major outlets like The New York Times give them a platform and allow them to be used to justify policies against Cuba."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83ea1082-20ee-4b63-85fa-168c52eb510d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Malcolm Jarrozai, an art professor at the University of Computer Sciences, speaks with Belly of the Beast journalist Liz Oliva Fern andez. Photo: Alfredo Lazcano Valera_

## **The Rise and Fall of Lourdes**
Construction of a Soviet signals intelligence (SIGINT) facility in Cuba[ began](https://substack.com/redirect/34369284-2f1e-42ab-8f88-7673a605ad06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as early as 1962, even before the Cuban Missile Crisis. By the 1980s,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2202823e-830c-4693-9147-1bff614b5d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)U.S. intelligence said Lourdes [was](https://substack.com/redirect/2202823e-830c-4693-9147-1bff614b5d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "the USSR's largest and most valuable base outside the Soviet Union for intelligence collection against the United States."
In a 1983 televised address, President Ronald Reagan[ cited](https://substack.com/redirect/87ab2e55-21f1-46a4-8740-707a84ec8625?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Lourdes as evidence of the Soviet threat to argue against proposed congressional budget cuts to defense spending. Reagan said the 28-square-mile base was manned by [1,500 Soviet technicians ](https://substack.com/redirect/f94a53fb-14a1-4292-a3d4-f475cef573ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and had grown by 60 percent in the previous decade. Two years later, the Departments of State and Defense[ estimated](https://substack.com/redirect/ce424279-d31d-42bd-9d28-82aee5198ffa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) there were as many as 14,700 Soviet personnel in Cuba, including 2,100 at Lourdes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dfc8d609-e278-4fec-9403-52abf14faea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_A photo of the wall of the Russian base known as Lourdes with satellite dishes in the background, before the base was dismantled. Photo: Rafael Torrabas._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b8dc307-4e51-49e1-be7c-611e0bfc3f5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_A map of the Lourdes base released by the U.S. government. Photo:[Federation of American Scientists](https://substack.com/redirect/34369284-2f1e-42ab-8f88-7673a605ad06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
Even after the fall of the Soviet Union, the Lourdes base remained in place to the consternation of neoconservatives and Cuban-American hardliners. In 1998, Jane's Intelligence Review[ wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/84cb8fa0-22d1-4ddb-b865-9918b497c7ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Lourdes remained "the greatest single overseas GRU [Russian military intelligence] asset" and[ provided](https://substack.com/redirect/5c38c0f8-3953-462b-8c61-138b10c205e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 60-70 percent of Russian electronic intelligence data on the United States. Two years later, a congressional report noted that[ there were](https://substack.com/redirect/84cb8fa0-22d1-4ddb-b865-9918b497c7ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) still more than 1,500 Russian engineers, technicians and military personnel at the base.
In January 2001, the hardline anti-Castro lawmaker Rep. Ileana Ros-Lehtinen (R-FL)[ introduced a bill](https://substack.com/redirect/b8ee1344-b1b0-453d-9b5b-8841ad173818?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would have prohibited forgiveness of Russian government debt until Lourdes was shuttered. Ten months later, Ros-Lehtinen, for whom Marco Rubio[ served as an intern](https://substack.com/redirect/861f8098-2a9f-40f1-83e2-1ec1ba60e7a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the early 1990s, got her wish.
On October 17, 2001, Russia's President Vladimir Putin[ announced](https://substack.com/redirect/884d4cc1-2b82-4805-9553-96dce9066935?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Russia would abandon Lourdes. U.S. President George W. Bush[ congratulated](https://substack.com/redirect/253fa85b-fd06-40f3-a507-3090a5b9b260?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Putin for taking down a "Cold War relic" and hailed the news as "another indication that the Cold War is over."
But other U.S. politicians have had a harder time letting go of the Cold War.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/87828843-65f4-4af3-8025-82eb03baf30b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Lourdes intelligence facility featured massive satellite dishes until Russia dismantled them when it closed the base between 2001 and 2002. Photos: Rafael Torrabas._
## **From Russia to China**
The closure of Lourdes didn't end talk of foreign spy bases in Cuba. Even before the Russians finally handed the base over to Cuban authorities in August 2002, El Nuevo Herald published [an article](https://substack.com/redirect/cb26b09e-9ed0-4b5e-83f5-3158f7bd8b2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) claiming that Lourdes had been replaced by a Chinese base at Bejucal, a town about seven miles away.
But allegations that China was using Cuba to spy on the United States did not become a national news story until 2023, when The Wall Street Journal __[ reported](https://substack.com/redirect/86ea5c34-c56f-4543-aff2-ed26be3fe25a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the two countries had reached a "secret agreement" for China to establish a spy base in Cuba. The Journal, citing anonymous officials "familiar with highly classified intelligence," said China had agreed "in principle" to pay Cuba "several billion dollars to allow it to build an eavesdropping station," and described the agreement as a "brash new geopolitical challenge" that has "sparked alarm" in the Biden administration.
A year later, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) released a[ report](https://substack.com/redirect/603e87a2-93f7-4edb-b44b-94e447f4a6b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that used commercial satellite imagery to identify four locations in Cuba, including Bejucal, "where China is most likely operating" its alleged spy bases.
The report, which was part of CSIS's "Hidden Reach" program to expose China's influence around the world, provided no evidence that the alleged spy bases in Cuba, even if real, were being operated by China. CSIS [recently acknowledged](https://substack.com/redirect/fd593b19-43c1-4f02-ac50-e189ce0cfdfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) there was "no clear publicly available evidence" proving China's presence at Bejucal.
"The report pulls the rumors and speculation in only one direction--to support its preordained conclusion that Chinese intelligence capabilities are expanding in ways threatening to U.S. interests, with Cuba's full support," said Fulton Armstrong, a former CIA analyst who also served as the nation's top intelligence officer on Latin America. "That's bad analysis."
Belly of the Beast [attempted to visit](https://substack.com/redirect/4f08b250-66c1-4d5b-b429-133d3625a2c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three of the four locations identified in the CSIS report. They appeared to be Cuban military installations but we found no evidence of heightened security or Chinese personnel.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4f08b250-66c1-4d5b-b429-133d3625a2c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
At one site, the guard posts appeared abandoned. Part of the facility's perimeter was lined with a rusty fence. Another section was bordered by trees. The main entrance was guarded by an elderly Cuban woman who was an unarmed civilian employed by Cuba's Vigilance and Protection Corps (CVP), a state agency that provides security services at schools, hospitals, stores, and hotels.
At another site, antennas draped in ivy and a dirt-covered satellite dish could be seen from the street.
"That's laughably old technology," said Armstrong after viewing video footage from two of the facilities. "It's sort of an insult to the Chinese if you're going to say that this is the future of their intel collection against the United States."
CSIS claimed the fourth location, near Santiago de Cuba, was being used to construct a circularly disposed antenna array (CDAA), a Cold War-era technology that [has become largely obsolete](https://substack.com/redirect/6e06e770-7cc2-4ea3-9eb5-5ec9fe3eb43b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The report itself acknowledges that Russia and the United States have abandoned most of their CDAAs.
A CSIS update to the report [published last month](https://substack.com/redirect/fd593b19-43c1-4f02-ac50-e189ce0cfdfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said construction had "largely ceased" and there was no indication the site was operational.
The CSIS report made no mention of a Russian spy base beyond noting that Lourdes had operated during the Cold War.
But Lourdes had nonetheless resurfaced in the news in 2014 amid heightened U.S.-Russian tensions, when The New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/264f5d7b-51df-4708-9999-6422b3b4658b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Russia had plans to reopen the base, [citing a Russian newspaper](https://substack.com/redirect/20fd3b3a-a635-4031-898d-06af8d52773d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Russian parliamentarians who "appeared to confirm the report." The next day, Putin [said](https://substack.com/redirect/eae79b4f-94f5-4d8f-8a74-9d73a31d8ed5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Russia had no such plans.
Not much was heard about the purported spy base until Trump's executive order revived the narrative that the Russians had returned to Cuba, though Rubio did mention Lourdes at a [2016 Republican primary debate](https://substack.com/redirect/e3ce493d-c7be-4611-b9fb-5eafe09af780?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Trump in Miami: "Here's a good deal...Cuba kicks out the Russians from Lourdes and kicks out the Chinese listening station in Bejucal."
In June [testimony](https://substack.com/redirect/55ca173c-1a4c-4932-bd57-16a938ec7078?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Rubio was asked for evidence supporting Cuba's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism.
"Cuba continues to host a pretty substantial collection of intelligence sites on behalf of the Chinese and the Russians," he said.
## **From Spy Base to Cuba 's Silicon Valley**
Cuban engineer Rafael Torralbas first stepped foot on the Russian base in April 2002. Torralbas and two other colleagues were tasked with creating a university within a matter of months.
"We had the challenge of receiving the installations being left behind by the Russian officials," said Torralbas. "There were huge [satellite dish] antennas, and I witnessed the process of dismantling them. There was technological equipment connected to the antennas, which we never saw. We knew it had been there, but the Russian officials had dismantled it all and they handed over the buildings completely empty."
Torralbas said the Russians removed "absolutely every antenna" along with everything else, including furniture and curtains. The Russians hauled the base's equipment home in six Antonov An-124 Ruslan cargo plane flights, according to Torralbas.
On September 23, 2002, one month after the last Russian left Lourdes, the University of Computer Sciences held its first classes on the grounds of the old base, which is located just two miles from Havana's Jose Marti International Airport.
In the following years, some of the Russian buildings were torn down, while others were repurposed. The apartment buildings housing the Russian personnel and their families were converted into residences for students and professors. A daycare center became a center for medical technology. A supermarket was turned into a library.
Torralbas now serves as the president of the[ Havana Science and Technology Park](https://substack.com/redirect/fb8395a6-bf11-4725-9c3a-2e6939454ee6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an innovation hub on the UCI campus that he says was inspired by Silicon Valley. Founded in 2020, the Technology Park serves as an incubator for Cuban tech startups, most of them private companies (despite[ claims to the contrary](https://substack.com/redirect/824c4158-feff-4d42-82b1-c0ef2b37af41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by hard-line politicians in Florida, Cuba's private sector has been thriving in recent years). The park also provides technological support to foreign and state-run companies.
Torralbas says the idea that Lourdes was reopened "could only exist in the mind of the person who made up that news."
"At no time, in this university, has anything existed that is not school buildings, students, computer science development centers, postgrad programs, that is, the normal activities of a university," he said. "It's shocking to me that someone in the intelligence community in the United States, with access to satellite images, could claim that a [spy base] exists here now."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9a39017e-11ea-4c8b-8622-779b75af1805?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The University of Computer Sciences, which occupies the grounds of the former Russian base known as Lourdes, has graduated thousands of students since it was founded in 2002. Photo: Alfredo Lazcano Valera_
## **Hunting for Russian Spies**
We spent hours walking around UCI's expansive tree-lined campus and drove around the perimeter, looking for any signs of signals intelligence or military installations. The security presence was minimal. We moved around freely and nobody seemed to care who we were or what we were doing. There was a guard at the entrance and two others in a far corner of the campus, where they watched over what appeared to be a side entrance--a partially closed door made of corrugated metal. The guards, who were unarmed, said they worked for a state-run security company. There were no military checkpoints.
According to Torralbas, more than 80% of the buildings on the campus were built since the Russians left 24 years ago. New classroom buildings, computer labs and research centers now occupy land where Soviet antennas once stood.
The only remnant of the old base we came across was a crumbling watchtower near the perimeter of the campus. It was impossible to ascend as its metal ladder had long since rusted away, leaving a small piece still visible at the top.
As for The New York Times' claim that the re-opened Lourdes "bristles with antennas"--we ultimately found two mobile phone antennas belonging to ETECSA, the state telecommunications company.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2f541fb-752b-4706-810b-10d6ee0ef4f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_One of the only antennas that is visible at the university. University staff say it is a mobile phone antenna owned by Cuba 's state-run telecommunications company. Photo: Reed Lindsa_
"We're in a rural area, so this is the only way we can have service for phone calls, text messages, internet, and everything else," explained Hector Gonzalez, a UCI graduate who now works in its communications department. "The antennas that were here [under the Russians] that were dismantled were different. They were enormous satellite dishes that you can see in some old photos, giant radars many meters high. These are just ordinary mobile network antennas."
The campus was mostly deserted. There are more than 2,500 undergraduate students currently enrolled at UCI, but only a handful were on campus.
The oil blockade has ground Cuba's public transportation to a halt. In February, with students and professors unable to get to class, Cuba's universities shifted to remote and hybrid instruction, suspending most in-person classes.
"It's a shame our students aren't here today," said Aylin Estrada, a UCI graduate and now a university dean who guided us around one of the newer school buildings, which has dozens of classrooms. "Normally these hallways are full of students, smiling, learning."
"Those buildings over there used to be for the people who worked [on the base]," said Franklin Quintana, a 37-year-old software developer, pointing to faded green five-story apartment buildings that now house university staff.
Quintana, who recently returned to the university to work as a software developer, shook his head when asked about the spy base.
"It's a false justification. There's no other way to understand it," he said.
"Rubio should come and look for it himself then. Look for it and prove it's here," said 68-year-old Estrella Luque, a school administrator whose daughter and son graduated from UCI and are now professors. "Cuba isn't a threat to anyone. I don't think anyone with two brain cells to rub together believes that."
After watching her children study and later teach at the university, Luque said she was sad to see the campus without students.
"They can say we're a failed state if they want...but no one can ignore or deny the impact of the blockade," said Luque. "A country like this little island, which has virtually no natural resources--we're not a major oil-producing island or a country with abundant resources--if you don't let oil in, naturally everything starts to fall apart. That's what's happening to us. But here we are. We keep going."

Since U.S. President Donald Trump imposed an executive order in January threatening tariffs on any country that ships fuel to Cuba, major media outlets have descended on the island to report on the resulting , , and . Far less attention has been paid to the rationale the administration offered for imposing the blockade in the first place. The states that Cuba represents a "national emergency" and poses an "unusual and extraordinary threat" to the United States, stringing together a kitchen-sink list of familiar allegations, including accusations that Cuba sponsors terrorism and aligns itself with "dangerous adversaries" of the United States, such as Iran, Hamas, Russia, and China. More specifically, the order claims that "Cuba hosts Russia's largest overseas signals intelligence facility, which tries to steal sensitive national security information of the United States." For two months, the allegation that Cuba was hosting a major Russian spy base was largely ignored by U.S. media outlets. Then, on March 24, The New York Times published an by Michael Crowley claiming not only that the Russian spy base exists, but that it "bristles with antennas and other eavesdropping equipment" capable of spying on the U.S. Central Command, the satellite launchpads of Cape Canaveral, and Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence. Crowley the location: a former Soviet base on the outskirts of Havana called Lourdes that was "temporarily shut" by Vladimir Putin in 2001 but was reopened in 2014, according to the Times. There is just one problem with this story: the base isn't there. The State Department did not respond to a request for comment. Belly of the Beast also sent requests to The New York Times and to Michael Crowley but received no response. Today, Lourdes (also known as Torrens) is home to Cuba's University of Computer Sciences (UCI). ** spent the better part of two days walking the campus, searching the grounds, and speaking with students, faculty, and workers. We found no evidence of an active Russian intelligence base, much less the sort of extensive equipment described by the Times. "Do I look like a Russian spy?" laughed Malcolm Jarrozai, a 40-year-old art professor who has been teaching at UCI and living at a residence on campus since 2006. Photos: Rafael Torrabas. From Russia to China The closure of Lourdes didn't end talk of foreign spy bases in Cuba. Even before the Russians finally handed the base over to Cuban authorities in August 2002, El Nuevo Herald published claiming that Lourdes had been replaced by a Chinese base at Bejucal, a town about seven miles away. But allegations that China was using Cuba to spy on the United States did not become a national news story until 2023, when The Wall Street Journal that the two countries had reached a "secret agreement" for China to establish a spy base in Cuba. The Journal, citing anonymous officials "familiar with highly classified intelligence," said China had agreed "in principle" to pay Cuba "several billion dollars to allow it to build an eavesdropping station," and described the agreement as a "brash new geopolitical challenge" that has "sparked alarm" in the Biden administration. A year later, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) released a that used commercial satellite imagery to identify four locations in Cuba, including Bejucal, "where China is most likely operating" its alleged spy bases. The report, which was part of CSIS's "Hidden Reach" program to expose China's influence around the world, provided no evidence that the alleged spy bases in Cuba, even if real, were being operated by China. CSIS there was "no clear publicly available evidence" proving China's presence at Bejucal. "The report pulls the rumors and speculation in only one direction--to support its preordained conclusion that Chinese intelligence capabilities are expanding in ways threatening to U.S. interests, with Cuba's full support," said Fulton Armstrong, a former CIA analyst who also served as the nation's top intelligence officer on Latin America. "That's bad analysis." Belly of the Beast three of the four locations identified in the CSIS report. They appeared to be Cuban military installations but we found no evidence of heightened security or Chinese personnel. At one site, the guard posts appeared abandoned. Part of the facility's perimeter was lined with a rusty fence. Another section was bordered by trees. The main entrance was guarded by an elderly Cuban woman who was an unarmed civilian employed by Cuba's Vigilance and Protection Corps (CVP), a state agency that provides security services at schools, hospitals, stores, and hotels. At another site, antennas draped in ivy and a dirt-covered satellite dish could be seen from the street. "That's laughably old technology," said Armstrong after viewing video footage from two of the facilities. "It's sort of an insult to the Chinese if you're going to say that this is the future of their intel collection against the United States." CSIS claimed the fourth location, near Santiago de Cuba, was being used to construct a circularly disposed antenna array (CDAA), a Cold War-era technology that . The report itself acknowledges that Russia and the United States have abandoned most of their CDAAs. A CSIS update to the report said construction had "largely ceased" and there was no indication the site was operational. The CSIS report made no mention of a Russian spy base beyond noting that Lourdes had operated during the Cold War. But Lourdes had nonetheless resurfaced in the news in 2014 amid heightened U.S.-Russian tensions, when The New York Times that Russia had plans to reopen the base, and Russian parliamentarians who "appeared to confirm the report." The next day, Putin Russia had no such plans. Not much was heard about the purported spy base until Trump's executive order revived the narrative that the Russians had returned to Cuba, though Rubio did mention Lourdes at a against Trump in Miami: "Here's a good deal...Cuba kicks out the Russians from Lourdes and kicks out the Chinese listening station in Bejucal." In June before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Rubio was asked for evidence supporting Cuba's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism. "Cuba continues to host a pretty substantial collection of intelligence sites on behalf of the Chinese and the Russians," he said. From Spy Base to Cuba 's Silicon Valley Cuban engineer Rafael Torralbas first stepped foot on the Russian base in April 2002. Torralbas and two other colleagues were tasked with creating a university within a matter of months. "We had the challenge of receiving the installations being left behind by the Russian officials," said Torralbas. "There were huge [satellite dish] antennas, and I witnessed the process of dismantling them. There was technological equipment connected to the antennas, which we never saw. We knew it had been there, but the Russian officials had dismantled it all and they handed over the buildings completely empty." Torralbas said the Russians removed "absolutely every antenna" along with everything else, including furniture and curtains. The Russians hauled the base's equipment home in six Antonov An-124 Ruslan cargo plane flights, according to Torralbas. On September 23, 2002, one month after the last Russian left Lourdes, the University of Computer Sciences held its first classes on the grounds of the old base, which is located just two miles from Havana's Jose Marti International Airport. In the following years, some of the Russian buildings were torn down, while others were repurposed. The apartment buildings housing the Russian personnel and their families were converted into residences for students and professors. A daycare center became a center for medical technology. A supermarket was turned into a library. Torralbas now serves as the president of the, an innovation hub on the UCI campus that he says was inspired by Silicon Valley. Founded in 2020, the Technology Park serves as an incubator for Cuban tech startups, most of them private companies (despite by hard-line politicians in Florida, Cuba's private sector has been thriving in recent years). The park also provides technological support to foreign and state-run companies. Torralbas says the idea that Lourdes was reopened "could only exist in the mind of the person who made up that news." "At no time, in this university, has anything existed that is not school buildings, students, computer science development centers, postgrad programs, that is, the normal activities of a university," he said. "It's shocking to me that someone in the intelligence community in the United States, with access to satellite images, could claim that a [spy base] exists here now." | | ---|---|--- The University of Computer Sciences, which occupies the grounds of the former Russian base known as Lourdes, has graduated thousands of students since it was founded in 2002. Photo: Alfredo Lazcano Valera Hunting for Russian Spies We spent hours walking around UCI's expansive tree-lined campus and drove around the perimeter, looking for any signs of signals intelligence or military installations. The security presence was minimal. We moved around freely and nobody seemed to care who we were or what we were doing. There was a guard at the entrance and two others in a far corner of the campus, where they watched over what appeared to be a side entrance--a partially closed door made of corrugated metal. The guards, who were unarmed, said they worked for a state-run security company. There were no military checkpoints. According to Torralbas, more than 80% of the buildings on the campus were built since the Russians left 24 years ago. New classroom buildings, computer labs and research centers now occupy land where Soviet antennas once stood. The only remnant of the old base we came across was a crumbling watchtower near the perimeter of the campus. It was impossible to ascend as its metal ladder had long since rusted away, leaving a small piece still visible at the top. As for The New York Times' claim that the re-opened Lourdes "bristles with antennas"--we ultimately found two mobile phone antennas belonging to ETECSA, the state telecommunications company. | | ---|---|--- One of the only antennas that is visible at the university. University staff say it is a mobile phone antenna owned by Cuba 's state-run telecommunications company. Photo: Reed Lindsa "We're in a rural area, so this is the only way we can have service for phone calls, text messages, internet, and everything else," explained Hector Gonzalez, a UCI graduate who now works in its communications department. "The antennas that were here [under the Russians] that were dismantled were different. They were enormous satellite dishes that you can see in some old photos, giant radars many meters high. These are just ordinary mobile network antennas." The campus was mostly deserted. There are more than 2,500 undergraduate students currently enrolled at UCI, but only a handful were on campus. The oil blockade has ground Cuba's public transportation to a halt. In February, with students and professors unable to get to class, Cuba's universities shifted to remote and hybrid instruction, suspending most in-person classes. "It's a shame our students aren't here today," said Aylin Estrada, a UCI graduate and now a university dean who guided us around one of the newer school buildings, which has dozens of classrooms. "Normally these hallways are full of students, smiling, learning." "Those buildings over there used to be for the people who worked [on the base]," said Franklin Quintana, a 37-year-old software developer, pointing to faded green five-story apartment buildings that now house university staff. Quintana, who recently returned to the university to work as a software developer, shook his head when asked about the spy base. "It's a false justification. There's no other way to understand it," he said. "Rubio should come and look for it himself then. Look for it and prove it's here," said 68-year-old Estrella Luque, a school administrator whose daughter and son graduated from UCI and are now professors. "Cuba isn't a threat to anyone. I don't think anyone with two brain cells to rub together believes that." After watching her children study and later teach at the university, Luque said she was sad to see the campus without students. "They can say we're a failed state if they want...but no one can ignore or deny the impact of the blockade," said Luque. "A country like this little island, which has virtually no natural resources--we're not a major oil-producing island or a country with abundant resources--if you don't let oil in, naturally everything starts to fall apart. That's what's happening to us. But here we are. We keep going." | A guest post by| Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. Trump’s judges just made it
easier for corporations to weaken unions.

Here's how it used to work: when one company bought another, workers kept
their union. The new owner had to recognize it and bargain in good faith
for at least a year before anyone could challenge it.

Not anymore.

Two Trump-appointed judges — Neomi Rao and Justin Walker — just threw that
protection out, clearing the way for new owners to challenge the union,
lower wages, and degrade working conditions almost immediately.

And they didn't do it alone. They used the Supreme Court's decision
gutting the Chevron doctrine — the rule that required courts to defer to
agency experts on tricky legal questions — to get there.

Now Trump's judges get to interpret labor law however they want, instead
of deferring to the agencies that actually enforce it. And they keep
twisting it in favor of corporations.

This is exactly what Trump's court takeover was built for: less power for
workers, more power for the corporations writing the checks and
bankrolling his corruption.

We’ve had enough. Demand Justice PAC is exposing Trump’s crony judges, the
corporate playbook, and the whole scheme to weaponize the courts against

name: Troy Jackson
subject: The fight for working-class Mainers
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260730_2.brWj02&refcode=em20260730-2&t=1001&akid=8027%2E582294%2EJVVQTj ]Troy Jackson

Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the
woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from
our government.

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has
sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too
dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.

My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation
logger.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260730_2.brWj02&refcode=em20260730-2&t=1002&akid=8027%2E582294%2EJVVQTj ]This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S.
Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers.
So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Chris Pappas
to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the
most important Senate race in the country.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260730_2.brWj02&refcode=em20260730-2&t=1003&akid=8027%2E582294%2EJVVQTj ]Donate Now »

Let me
tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My
family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I
was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my
mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad
before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and
me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians,
including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but
they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change
unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six
years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life
to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol,
because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district
that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about
a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

I’m
building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks
like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate
class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas
tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be
determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every
working family in Maine has the government they deserve.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260730_2.brWj02&refcode=em20260730-2&t=1004&akid=8027%2E582294%2EJVVQTj ]If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to
split a donation between my campaign and Chris Pappas today to help us
reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions. Even $5 makes a
difference »

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260730_2.brWj02&amount=5&refcode=em20260730-2&t=1023&akid=8027%2E582294%2EJVVQTj ]Donate $5 »

In solidarity with you always,

Troy Jackson

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it. My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger. [ ]This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Chris Pappas to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. [ ]Donate Now » Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me. When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us. After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power. So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people. I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family. I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve. [ ]If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Chris Pappas today to help us reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions. Even $5 makes a difference » [ ]Donate $5 » In solidarity with you always, Troy Jackson You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

**That’s why I’m proud to support Deb to be our next governor.**
I’ve worked with Deb Haaland a long time, and I can tell you this: Deb is incredibly kind, leads with compassion, and cares deeply about New Mexico and the people who call it home.
Deb has spent her career standing up for our communities, protecting our public lands, defending reproductive rights, and fighting for working families. She understands what New Mexicans are going through because she’s lived it herself — a single mom, a former small business owner, someone who knows what it means to work hard and still struggle to get by.
She’s ready to lead New Mexico forward, and I know we’ll work together to deliver for the people of our state.

| | Dear Peter,
The Green Party of Washington has formally endorsed independent socialist Kshama Sawant for U.S. Congress in Washington’s 9th District. Kshama is challenging incumbent Democrat Adam Smith, a genocidal warmonger who has been in office for 29 years.
The Kshama Sawant campaign met with the Green Party of Washington on July 14, 2026, to mobilize to get out the vote for the August 4th primary election and plan mutual support.
Kshama is the socialist who won landmark victories for working people as a Seattle City Councilmember by building movements to fight and defeat the billionaire class and their political servants. We need all hands on deck in the coming weeks to turn out the vote by August 4th so that she can advance to November’s general election for a head-to-head against Adam Smith.
“The Green Party of Washington has formally and proudly endorsed Kshama Sawant for Congress in the 9th District,” announced Marc Mixon, Chair of the Green Party of Washington, following the July 14th meeting.
In addition, the Green Party of Washington and its local Seattle chapter have an ambitious plan to field Green Party candidates for the 2027 Seattle City Council elections in all seven districts. Beginning in 2027, Seattle City Council elections will be conducted by ranked choice voting.
“I’m excited about joining the Green Party and supporting its plans in Seattle and around the state, and I am grateful for the party’s endorsement of my campaign for Congress,” said Kshama, whose grassroots campaigns won multiple terms to Seattle City Council and defeated a billionaire-funded recall effort.
In solidarity,Justin Bare, Campaign Manager of Kshama for CongressMarc Mixon, Green Party of Washington State Chair

#### Logger-Turned-Senate Hopeful Troy Jackson and Longtime Squeeze Lana Pelletier Are Second Cousins by Blood -- and the Pair Has Never Bothered with a Marriage License
**ALLAGASH --** The tiny St. John River Valley town of Allagash (population 240) has long been the butt of Maine jokes about its handful of last names and family trees that don't so much branch as tangle.
Now Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Troy
Dale Jackson, 58, and on his fifth pacemaker, finds his own ancestry under the same microscope that eventually ran his predecessor, oyster hobbyist Graham Platner, out of American politics and into hiding.
Jackson, a 26-year politician and lobbyist, has made a career of bragging that he's a is a fifth-generation logger, but you don't have to go far back the generational line to find where it crosses paths with the ancestors of his significant other Lana M. Pelletier
Troy D. Jackson, 16, Fork Kent High School Yearbook, 1983
Lana Pelletier, The 1982 Fort Kent High School Yearbook
Allagash tipsters and genealogical records confirm that Jackson's longtime significant other, Lana Pelletier -- his high school sweetheart and the mother of his two adult sons, Chace and Camden -- is, in fact, his second cousin by blood.
Jackson and Pelletier share the same great-grandparents: Thomas Pelletier and Edith Thibodeau. Thomas and Edith's daughter Albertine was Troy's grandmother; their son Louis Sr. was Lana's grandfather. That makes Troy and Lana second cousins on the Pelletier line.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..OUWF0dmccPBEiVcVr7UxL07wacseA0bDjxg3GD3vseI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=209142787)
The pair has been together for Jackson's entire political career, stretching from his early days as a pro-gun, pro-life, conservative working-class rabble-rouser in the late 1990s and early 2000s through his rise to become a pro-gun-control, pro-late-term-abortion socialist state Senate president.
Pelletier has eschewed the spotlight, slugging along at various state jobs while Jackson has pursued his political ambitions and lucrative side hustles as the political enforcer for Maine's dwindling labor movement.
Now, his sudden elevation as the Democratic nominee to challenge Republican Sen. Susan Collins has brought renewed focus to both candidates, with left-wing muckrakers circulating conspiracy theories about Sen. Collins' love life and the retirement investments of her husband. But the more curious significant-other story in the Senate race might just be the Aroostook romance that could have taken root at an Allagash family reunion.
Jackson has, at various points, referred to Pelletier as his wife in official bios and statements. Locals in the historically Catholic village of Allagash, however, are quick to set the record straight with the dry precision of people who have known both families -- or just the one family, depending on your perspective -- for generations: The couple is not, and has never been, legally married.
They simply live together, raise kids together and appear together on the occasional mortgage and lawsuit paperwork. In a place where everyone knows everyone's business, the lack of a marriage certificate is less a scandal than local trivia.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/06e7d98e-a13a-4acf-9cea-4a4a32a8e297?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Family Wreath: Jackson and Pelletier 's common great-grandparents were Thomas Pelletier and Edith Thibodeau Pelletier. Thomas and Edith had two children who matter here: Albertine Pelletier O'Leary and Louis A. Pelletier Sr. Albertine was the mother of Colleen McBreairty, and Colleen was the mother of Troy Jackson. Louis Sr. was the father of Louis A. "Louie" Pelletier Jr. Louie Jr. and his wife, Patricia "Patty" Gardner Pelletier, were Lana Pelletier's parents. That means Colleen McBreairty and Louie Pelletier Jr. were first cousins. Their children, Troy Jackson and Lana Pelletier, are second cousins because they share the same great-grandparents: Thomas and Edith Pelletier._
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=209142787&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MTQyNzg3LCJpYXQiOjE3ODU0NDAzMjIsImV4cCI6MTc4ODAzMjMyMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.1Of4mET90XRedrMdamiROrP_3QywBvoRlAOt-uYpWpM)
## Second Cousins, Not First: The Critical Distinction
Before the pearl-clutching begins, let's be precise -- because the difference between first-cousin and second-cousin relationships is both legal and biological, and Maine law draws a bright line.
First cousins share a pair of grandparents. They inherit, on average, about 12.5 percent of their DNA from the same recent ancestors. That shared genetic material raises the risk of recessive genetic disorders in any children roughly twofold compared with the general population -- from a baseline of about 2-3 percent for major birth defects to roughly 4-6 percent, according to reviews by the National Society of Genetic Counselors and studies published in the _Journal of Genetic Counseling_.
In short, Western man has, for millennia, tabooed first-cousin marriage because the progeny of such unions frequently exhibit physical deformities and severe cognitive impairment. That's part of why Pakistani culture -- both in Pakistan and in the British Isles, which Pakistani people have been colonizing for half a century -- is notoriously maligned for astronomically high rates of consanguinity, a cultural fact that has materialized across the U.K. with obvious consequences.
Maine law reflects the concern that Pakistani-style incest should be prohibited. Bizarrely, the law was introduced only during the Reagan administration.
In 1985, the 112th Maine Legislature passed LD 873/H.P. 603, titled "An Act to Prohibit Marriage Between Certain Blood Relatives." It was enacted as Public Law 1985, Chapter 181, and took effect on September 19, 1985. Under Title 19-A, §701 of the Maine Revised Statutes, marriage between first cousins is prohibited -- but not completely.
First cousins who find their love destined in the stars can obtain a physician's certificate of genetic counseling. That's thanks to an amendment two years later that created a pathway for familial lovers who really wanted to test the genetic lottery. The counseling requirement has been on the books since the mid-1980s, with clarifying language added in the 1990s, making Maine one of the few states that permits first-cousin marriage if Dr. Deliverance signs the permission slip.
Second cousins, by contrast, share a pair of great-grandparents. Their coefficient of relationship is only about 3.125 percent -- roughly a quarter of the first-cousin figure. Geneticists regard the elevated risk of recessive disorders as negligible compared with the risk for closer cousins.
Maine imposes no special restrictions on second-cousin marriage; it is treated like any other union between consenting adults. Jackson and Pelletier fall squarely into this second category -- should they ever decide to formally get hitched.
Family records and local knowledge in Allagash identify them as the children of first cousins: Jackson's mother, Colleen (O'Leary) McBreairty, and Pelletier's father are first cousins through the Pelletier line that runs deep in the St. John Valley.
That makes the couple second cousins by blood -- close enough for small-town knowing glances, distant enough that the law and biology shrug.
## American Politics' Long, Awkward History with Cousins
If the revelation feels awkward in 2026, American political history offers a robust, if slightly squirm-inducing, context. Cousin marriage -- or at least cousin coupling -- is practically a Founding-era tradition, practiced by figures far more exalted than a logger-lobbyist who now makes his home in Augusta.
John Adams, the second president, married Abigail Smith, his third cousin. Thomas Jefferson married Martha Wayles Skelton, also his third cousin. Martin Van Buren wed Hannah Hoes, his first cousin once removed. Franklin D. Roosevelt married Eleanor Roosevelt, his fifth cousin once removed -- a degree of relatedness so remote that geneticists treat it as essentially unrelated, yet still close enough that the Roosevelt name stayed comfortably in the family.
John Adams' grandson, John Adams II, married his first cousin, Mary Catherine Hellen, in a White House ceremony. Alabama Gov. Bibb Graves married his first cousin, Dixie Bibb. Even modern figures have gotten in on the act: Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani's first marriage was to Regina Peruggi, his second cousin once removed.
The practice was once common among the Anglo-American elite for the same reasons it persists in many traditional societies: keeping property, status and political alliances inside the extended family. It acquired its modern stigma only in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, as genetic science advanced and Progressive Era reformers began targeting "inbreeding" among the rural poor and certain immigrant groups.
By the time Maine adjusted its statutes in the 1980s, the cultural taboo had hardened, even as the actual genetic risk for second cousins remained trivial.
## The Allagash Reality Check
In Allagash itself, the Jackson-Pelletier arrangement has been an open secret for decades. The couple's two sons are grown. Pelletier works as a clinical care specialist with the Maine Department of Health and Human Services. Jackson has built a political brand on being the authentic working-class guy from the far north woods.
The fact that his domestic partner is also a blood relative of the second-cousin variety may strike outsiders as the punchline to a _Deliverance_ joke. The comparisons between Appalachia and Allagash write themselves.
To locals who have watched the same surnames -- Pelletier, McBreairty, Jackson and O'Leary -- recycle through town records for generations, it is simply another data point in a place where the dating pool is shallower than the trout streams.
Jackson has never publicly addressed the cousin connection. His campaign materials continue to describe Pelletier as his "partner." Older official bios occasionally slipped into "wife."
In the grand tradition of American politics, where presidents married their cousins and the republic somehow survived, Troy Jackson and Lana Pelletier's arrangement is less a scandal than a footnote written in the fine print of a very small town's genealogy.
Where the relationship between Jackson and Pelletier may have real political consequences comes down to the rules of the secretary of the U.S. Senate, who handles the financial disclosures that candidates and elected members of Congress are required to submit.

Typically, pols must submit detailed accounts of their income, assets and liabilities, as well as the finances of their spouses. But because Pelletier and Jackson never wed, and because Maine does not recognize any form of common-law marriage, it's not clear whether Jackson's financial disclosures will cover the second-cousin couple's full financial situation.
If Pelletier, as merely the mother of Jackson's adult children, is exempt from inclusion in the financial disclosures in a way that Collins' husband is not, then the knitted family tree could engage in all kinds of clever accounting tricks to artificially impoverish Jackson as a way of maintaining his working-class image.
As of this week, Jackson hasn't filed the disclosures or a request for an extension, and the circumstances of his nomination are so unusual that the secretary of the Senate has yet to say when Jackson will be required to make his finances transparent -- or whether those disclosures will include assets placed under the name of his second cousin.

**The heart of America depends on Arizona.**

That's not a slogan. It's the map. Whoever controls Arizona controls the path to the White House, the Senate, and the future of this country.

We've said it for years, and this week, the voters of Arizona proved they believe it, too.

**But a primary win isn 't the finish line. It's the starting gun.**

Right now, we have our people hitting the pavement, doing the clipboard-and-tennis-shoes work to turn out as many voters as possible this election.

name: Dan Osborn
subject: If I win in November, I will be the least wealthy member of the U.S. Senate.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-osborn?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-osborn?amount=25]
The U.S. Senate is a country club. It’s full of billionaires, former business execs, lawyers with Ivy League degrees, and trust fund kids born with so many silver spoons in their mouths that they have no idea the reality for working-class people like me.
If I defeat my opponent, the literal billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts, I will be the least wealthy member of the U.S. Senate. I don’t come from money, and I’m not rich. I’m a steamfitter and mechanic who’s worked 50 and 60-hour workweeks my whole life to give my kids a better life.
I will be the only senator without a college degree. After my wife and I found out we were expecting a baby, I had to drop out and kill my dream of hanging a diploma on the wall because my family needed health insurance, diapers, and food on the table.
I will be the only senator who is a blue-collar, card-carrying, union member. When Kellogg’s tried to cut our benefits and workers’ pay, we risked it all, went on strike, and walked the picket line for 11 weeks through the bitter cold Nebraska winter. We won and saved hundreds of good-paying jobs – before I was fired for being the union president who led the strike.
There is no one who represents working-class people like me in the U.S. Senate. But in 2024, ours was one of the closest Senate races in the country. And the latest poll for 2026 shows me LEADING Republican Pete Ricketts in 2026 – 47% to 46%.
I’ve taken on a big corporation before and won, and now I’m going to defeat a literal billionaire – my opponent Republican Pete Ricketts – and win this Senate seat. But I need your help to do it.
We’ve set big fundraising goals, but I’m not taking money from corporate PACs like my opponent. If I’m going to defeat Republican Pete Ricketts and win this Senate seat, I need grassroots donors like you to give right now:
I have nowhere else to turn. Please, will you donate to Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign right now – every dollar you can afford – to help me defeat Republican Pete Ricketts and flip this Senate seat? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-osborn?amount=25]

Another amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-osborn?express_lane=true&amount=other]
I’m ready to be the 51st vote in the Senate to take on the billionaires and corporations, fight for working-class people, and expand workers’ rights – but I can’t do it without you.
I know the value of a dollar, so I am grateful for any amount you can afford to give. It genuinely means a lot to me.
Thank you for being a part of the team,
Dan Osborn

| | David, Hereʼs a fact thatʼs sad but true. Most politicians and DC consultants do not have a very high opinion of votersʼ intelligence. Yup, I said it: they think voters are pretty dumb. So why would I send a letter as my first mailer? Isnʼt that a lot to read? Do we really think voters are going to take the time to look at all that? **Yes. I do.** [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SoR-KVo79jHV6OLBXPK-cA~~/AAUS1hA~/U2zcwwMLlN_4-pr-FR8r13NRKHn_OguLLK-CTzS7LVB142ck59aCkdK3FZL_SjLHlVuQTfcIK2I0ah1gNN_UpBAWSNKtaNB-q812D6Jltk8Cxd8gwVNfypVr39SDOyFvBkZZgHMgaaUWq6H7lsYwcT3YhBJe-kCXATSZbaIXzGClny2gbJtwEWpNOtC7RUEOFTw7wVJ_LOEfmAwBKnxwsuQVo2bNQEfD3EhjTkCDCmDTE9Le_-eKvzbx1O1hJ2BW5TUt4hz49Af2F_njDbcWaw~~) For way too long, politicians on both sides of the aisle have treated voters like sheep. Talked down to us. Demeaned us. Treated us like our lived experience and ideas donʼt matter. 24-hour cable news doesnʼt help. Neither does social media. Politicians and political consultants assume that voters lack the attention span to process nuance or complexity, so they start talking at us like we lack the intelligence to participate in the decisions that affect our daily lives. **_And thatʼs how we get clown shows like the Fauci hearing yesterday._** But I learned something as a teacher: when you respect the people you work with enough to tell them the whole story, and you tell it truthfully, people rise to meet our expectations. # [Seagulls at the Cherry Festival](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=209120161&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MTIwMTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU0NDE5ODIsImV4cCI6MTc4ODAzMzk4MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.z2dcKOBZgU86KmcymtGQ4UPu_z-hdAvGmEjjPKKoiSs)
### I know it's annoying, but tomorrow is our final end-of-month fundraising deadline before the primary, and I need your help.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 30
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/seagulls-at-the-cherry-festival?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MTIwMTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU0NDE5ODIsImV4cCI6MTc4ODAzMzk4MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.z2dcKOBZgU86KmcymtGQ4UPu_z-hdAvGmEjjPKKoiSs&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/seagulls-at-the-cherry-festival?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
Summer is the absolute best in Michigan. You're sitting by the lake, relaxing, pulling snacks out of the cooler - and then a seagull locks eyes with you from 20 feet away. Just checking in. Making sure you're good, hovering a little. Hoping you can throw something their way. It can be mildly annoying.
Right now, this campaign can feel like a seagull at the lake.
If it feels like you've been hearing from us a LOT lately - texts, ads in the middle of the Tigers game, on the news, in the paper - you're not imagining things. You have. I know.
I see the messages too, and yeah, I find them a little annoying, and I'm the one sending them!
I'm not going to pretend asking for money is my favorite part of the job. But this is a grassroots campaign, and I wouldn't ask if I didn't absolutely need your support. **The truth is, we 're in the last stretch of the most important Senate primary in the country.**
**[Your $10 or $20](https://substack.com/redirect/60717eb7-5bf2-42fc-95e0-dab6fd7de0c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** can truly make a difference in keeping Michigan blue. This is the part of a primary where you find out what our team is made of. Where every hour, every volunteer, every dollar, every Substack matters.
Here's why I'm writing to you right now: Tomorrow at midnight is our final end-of-month deadline before the primary. And the primary is five days away.
I've written to you about FEC deadlines before - those were about numbers going public. This one is different, and it's simpler. This one is all about the calendar.
Here's what I mean: Whatever we raise by tomorrow night is money we can actually use - THIS week, while Michiganders still have ballots on their kitchen tables or are getting ready to head to the polls. That's the whole thing. If we don't hit our end-of-month goal, there's no next month. There's no next stretch. There's only five days left.
And I want to be specific about what your money does in these five days, because I think you deserve to know exactly what you're buying and why I'm being a little pushy:
**It keeps our TV ad on the air.** One ad airing during prime time costs more than $2,000. That's one shot at one living room. Our ad talks about my record, shows receipts, and tells Michiganders that at the end of the day, I'm in this 100% for THEM.
**It knocks doors.** In a race this close, the people who decide it are the ones somebody actually talked to. Your contribution helps keep our organizers around the state working every hour to reach voters where they are.
**It answers the other side.** MAGA Mike Rogers has a Texas oil billionaire, the Koch network, and the full weight of the national Republican machine behind him. He recently sent out a fundraising email asking Michiganders to give him money so he can "protect Elon" Musk. That's who we're up against: a Florida millionaire raising money to shield the richest man on Earth while folks across this state are struggling to afford to fill their tanks.
Look, I'm the only non-millionaire in this race. I can't self-fund. I don't have a wealthy father-in-law like my opponent. What I have is you, and that's the point. That's why I'm in this. For regular, hardworking folks.
Polls show I'm the strongest Democrat to beat Mike Rogers in November - and I'm doing especially well with independents, a critical group in Michigan. The nonpartisan _The Cook Political Report_ put it pretty bluntly: "If El-Sayed wins the primary, Democrats have little chance of holding the seat."
That's why Governor Gretchen Whitmer endorsed me. It's why Senator Gary Peters, who has held this seat for 12 years, asked Michigan to send me to finish what he started. It's why Congressman Jim Clyburn, former Senator Debbie Stabenow, EMILYs List, the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, and 20 unions are with me. Those folks have spent their careers winning tough races in this state. They looked at this one, they did the math, and they chose to stand with me. I'm grateful.
It matters because Senate control could very well come down to what Michigan does on Aug. 4. Are we giving Democrats the best possible chance to beat Florida Mike? Or does Michigan turn red in November?
**[Here 's my direct ask, and then I'll get out of your hair: Will you chip in $20 before midnight on Friday, July 31, to help us finish these last five days at full strength?](https://substack.com/redirect/60717eb7-5bf2-42fc-95e0-dab6fd7de0c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/60717eb7-5bf2-42fc-95e0-dab6fd7de0c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you've already given, thank you. Truly. I'm honored that you'd trust me to go to the U.S. Senate and fight for you.
Believe me when I say I know there are folks reading this who are stretched thin, who've got their own bills to worry about, and who are frankly tired of every politician in America asking them for $5. I get it. I really do. Seagulls can be annoying.
If that's you, please don't give me a dime. Just do me a favor and, if you're in Michigan, go vote. And tell a friend why you're checking the box for Haley. That's the part that actually decides this.
Last thing. I've been running this race for over a year - knocking on doors, hanging out in diners, talking to folks in union halls, walking picket lines - and I've never felt anything like these last few weeks. Folks are fired up and ready to go. It's momentum. It's enthusiasm. It's joy and stick it to 'em.
I love this state so much.
Michiganders are standing up to say we want a fighter. We want to keep this state blue. We want somebody who gets stuff done.
That's me. I promise I won't let you down.
Five days, friends. Full speed ahead. Pedal to the metal.
More soon.
With gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/60717eb7-5bf2-42fc-95e0-dab6fd7de0c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

We want to keep this state blue. We want somebody who gets stuff done. That's me. I promise I won't let you down. Five days, friends. Full speed ahead. Pedal to the metal. More soon. With gratitude, Haley A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

We’re guessing your inbox is probably filled with end-of-month fundraising emails right now, each one more panicked-sounding than the last (we get those, too — and immediately delete them).
Overly dramatic emails aren’t just cringe-inducing, they can be disingenuous and dishonest, too, using a false sense of urgency, unrealistic promises, and made-up deadlines to compel people to donate.
So as a rule, we don’t send those! Instead, we want to be 100% transparent about why the next few days and weeks matter so much:
We’re heading into the final stretch of the summer, when no one wants to spend more time reading emails and clearing out their inboxes than is absolutely necessary.
But there’s also the reality that tomorrow (July 31st) is one of our last internal benchmarks before the midterms begin in earnest — voting starts in California in just 67 days!
Every dollar we raise right now helps us enter this critical final stretch in the strongest possible position — and get ready to win big.
Sara is running in a more competitive district under California’s new congressional maps, while also helping support Democrats across the country to flip the House. All of that requires serious planning and resources before voting begins. A strong July puts Sara in a position to build the kind of operation she’ll need in August, September, and October to compete and win.
So here’s the ask: If you’re in a position to contribute to Sara’s campaign, will you make a donation before the end of the month? Our average online donation right now is $26 — plenty give less, some give more — but truly, any amount helps. Here's a link you can use:
